newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Ssangyong Oil to raise guarantees to car affiliate.
newsitem.headline: Ssangyong Oil to raise guarantees to car affiliate.

text.p: South Korea's Ssangyong Oil Refining Co has decided to raise payment guarantees to its affiliate Ssangyong Motor to 180 billion won from 100 billion, a Ssangyong Group spokesman said on Friday.

Ssangyong Oil, the major shareholder of its automobile affiliate, was able to make the decision after the refiner's major shareholder, Saudi Arabia's state-oil company Saudi Aramco, agreed to the guarantee hike, he said.
The spokeman said Ssangyong Oil has a 33.3 percent stake in Ssangyong Motor and Saudi Aramco owns 35 percent of the refiner.

He said Ssangyong Motor planned to convert 100 billion won worth of Ssangyong Motor convertible bonds to stocks next month and issue an additional 100 billion won worth of convertible bonds in the second half of this year.
"This will improve Ssangyong Motor's financial status and solve the current fund shortage," he said.
Analysts said the conversion of convertible bonds would increase Ssangyong Motor's shareholders' equity and improve its debt-to-equity ratio.

"The conversion of convertible bonds could help the company look better for financial institutions when they go through the credit screening process," said Kim Byong-suk, a banking analyst at Hannuri-Salomon Securities.
Ssangyong Motor has suffered from huge losses, a result of massive investments in new models.
Ssangyong's debts are currently estimated at 3.2 trillion won. The nation's four-wheel-drive utility vehicle maker incurred losses of 228.5 billion won in 1996 on sales of 1.37 trillion won.
Ssangyong Motor's debt-to-equity ratio stood at 10,496 percent at the end of last year, according to Korea Investor's service.
